name: Nine Men’s Morris
intro: Learn Nine Men’s Morris from scratch: the board, placing, mills, moving and flying, then blocking, flexible placing, the running mill and the flying endgame.

units.name: How Nine Men’s Morris works
units.blurb: The board, placing, mills, moving, flying and how you win.

lessons.title: The Nine Men’s Morris board
lessons.summary: Nine Men’s Morris is played on 24 points joined by lines, with nine pieces each. Learn the board, where mills can form and who moves first.
lessons.wrap: That’s the board. Next: making a mill.

steps.text:
The board has 24 points on three squares, one inside the other, joined by four short lines across the middle of each side.

Each player has nine pieces, which start off the board. Gold moves first.
Three points in a straight line along a side of a square, like the top edge here, or along one of the joining lines, can make a mill. There are 16 possible mills.
Quick check.
steps.prompt: How many pieces does each player have?

steps.text: The game starts with placing: players take turns putting one piece on any empty point.

lessons.title: Making a mill and removing a piece
lessons.summary: Three of your pieces in a line is a mill, and every new mill lets you remove one of your opponent’s pieces. Learn the rule, and which pieces you can take.
lessons.wrap: Mills remove pieces, but pieces in a mill are protected. Next: moving and flying.

steps.text: When you make a mill, three of your pieces in a line, you remove one of your opponent’s pieces from the board.
You have two pieces on the top line.
steps.prompt: Make a mill, then tap an ivory piece to remove it.
steps.wrong: Complete the line of three along the top.
steps.done: A mill! One ivory piece is gone.

steps.text:
Pieces in a mill are protected: you can’t remove one unless all of your opponent’s pieces are in mills.

You’ve just made a mill.
steps.prompt: Tap every ivory piece you’re allowed to remove.
steps.wrong: That piece is part of Ivory’s mill along the bottom.
steps.done: Right: only the two pieces outside the mill.

steps.text: And if every ivory piece is in a mill?
steps.explain: Yes. When all of your opponent’s pieces are in mills, you can take any of them.

lessons.title: Moving and flying
lessons.summary: Once all 18 pieces are placed, you move along the lines to a neighbouring point. With three pieces left, you can fly anywhere. Learn both.
lessons.wrap: Moving makes and breaks mills; flying makes three pieces dangerous. Next: how to win.

steps.text: When all the pieces are placed, players take turns moving one piece along a line to a neighbouring empty point. A mill made by moving removes a piece too.
Tap your piece, then the point to move it to.
steps.wrong: Move a piece along a line to finish the top line of three.

position.ivory: a7 d7 f6 e5 c5 b4

steps.text: A player with only three pieces left may fly: move a piece to any empty point, not just a neighbouring one.

position.ivory: a7 d7 f6 e5 c5 b4

steps.text: You have three pieces, so you can fly.
steps.prompt: Fly a piece to make a mill.
steps.wrong: Your two pieces along the bottom line need a third. Fly your other piece there.

lessons.title: How to win Nine Men’s Morris
lessons.summary: You win Nine Men’s Morris by reducing your opponent to two pieces, or leaving them with no legal move. Learn both, and the draw rules.
lessons.wrap: You know all the rules. Test yourself in the rules check.

steps.text: You win when your opponent is down to two pieces, because they can’t make a mill any more. You also win if they have no legal move, with every piece blocked in.
Ivory has three pieces left.
steps.wrong: Make a mill, and the piece you remove leaves Ivory with two.
steps.done: Ivory is down to two pieces. You win!

steps.text: And if nobody can win?
steps.prompt: When is it a draw here?
options: The same position three times, or 50 moves each with nothing removed
When both players have three pieces
steps.explain: Both of those are draws on BoardGameSite, so a game can’t go on for ever.

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Five questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the strategy.

lessons.title: Nine Men’s Morris rules check
lessons.summary: Test your Nine Men’s Morris rules: placing, making mills, which pieces you can remove, flying with three pieces and how to win.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for the strategy.

steps.text: Question 1.
steps.prompt: Make a mill, then remove a piece.
steps.wrong: Finish your line up the left side.

steps.text: Question 2. You’ve made a mill.
steps.prompt: Tap every ivory piece you may remove.
steps.wrong: That piece is in Ivory’s mill.

steps.text: Question 3.
options: When they have three pieces left

steps.text: Question 4.
steps.wrong: A mill now leaves Ivory with two pieces.

steps.text: Question 5.
steps.prompt: What happens if you can’t move any piece?
steps.explain: You lose. Being blocked in is a way to lose with plenty of pieces left.

units.name: Strategy
units.blurb: Flexible placing, blocking, running mills and the endgame.

lessons.title: Block two in a row
lessons.summary: When your opponent has two pieces in a line with the third point empty, block it before it becomes a mill. Practise spotting the threat.
lessons.wrap: Block two-in-a-rows, unless you can make a mill yourself first.

steps.text: Ivory has two pieces along the bottom line, and the third point is empty. Next turn that’s a mill, and you lose a piece.
You’re still placing pieces.
steps.wrong: Ivory can still finish the line. Put your piece on its empty point.

lessons.title: Place on the busy points
lessons.summary: Some points on the Morris board touch four others, and some only two. Learn why flexible points matter more than quick mills while placing.
lessons.wrap: Flexible pieces make more mills later than quick mills made early.

steps.text:
While placing, quick mills are easy to see and easy to block. Strong players put pieces where they can join several possible mills and move freely later.

The points in the middle of each side of the middle square connect to the most other points.
Look at the lines from each point.
steps.prompt: Tap every point that connects to four others.
steps.wrong: That point has fewer lines. Look at the middle square.
steps.done: Those four points connect to the most others.

lessons.title: The running mill
lessons.summary: A mill you can open and close again with one piece removes a piece every other turn. Learn to close a running mill.
lessons.wrap: Open your mill when it’s safe, and close it again next turn.

steps.text:
A running mill is a mill where one piece can step out and back in. Every time it closes, you remove a piece.

Last turn you moved a piece out of your mill at the bottom of the middle line. No ivory piece is next to the empty point, so Ivory couldn’t block it.
Close the mill again.
steps.prompt: Make the mill and remove a piece.
steps.wrong: Move your piece back into the gap in your line.
steps.done: Closed. Next turn you can open it again.

lessons.title: Defending against a flying opponent
lessons.summary: A player with three pieces can fly anywhere, so every two-in-a-row is a threat. Learn to block a flying opponent.
lessons.wrap: Against a flying opponent, watch every pair of their pieces.

steps.text: Ivory is down to three pieces, so Ivory can fly. Any two ivory pieces in a line with the third point empty can become a mill next turn.
Ivory’s top line needs one more piece.
steps.wrong: Ivory can still fly into the top line. Move a piece onto the empty point.
